abstract.p: This paper describes our submissions to the TSAR 2025 Shared Task on Readability-Controlled Text Simplification. We present a comparative study of three architectures: a rule-based Baseline, a heuristic-driven Expert system, and a zero-shot generative T5 Pipeline with a semantic guardrail. Our analysis of the official results shows a clear trade-off between the controllability of rulebased systems and the fluency of generative models. We detect that in this zero-shot instance, our simpler, confined systems achieved superior meaning preservation scores compared to the powerful but less predictable generative model. We present a diagnostic failure analysis centered in our actual system outputs, illustrating how different architectural choices result distinct error patterns, such as undersimplification, information loss via heuristics, and semantic drift.
